headline: Kansai Electric and Kawasaki Heavy to trial Japan's first off-site transport of captured CO2
summary: Kansai Electric Power and Kawasaki Heavy Industries plan to move CO2 captured at the Maizuru coal-fired power plant to a remote location as early as this fiscal year, aiming to establish an off-site CO2 transport-and-storage chain.
co2crc_note: Off-site CO2 transport from a point source mirrors the hub-and-transport logistics CO2CRC studies for Australian sources feeding Otway-type storage.

headline: EU's first offshore CCS project, Denmark's Greensand, nears launch
summary: Upstream reports the launch of Project Greensand — INEOS Energy's depleted-reservoir CO2 storage development in the Danish North Sea, set to be the EU's first offshore CCS project — is 'imminent', with an initial injection target of about 0.4 Mtpa.
co2crc_note: First operational EU offshore storage is a live reference case for Australia's offshore storage ambitions (Bayu-Undan, CarbonNet) and shipped-CO2 value chains.

headline: The world is cooling on carbon capture — why is Canada barreling ahead?
summary: A Globe and Mail commentary argues international enthusiasm for CCS is fading even as Canada continues to back major projects, questioning the strategy and public spending behind them.
co2crc_note: Social-licence signal: a mainstream sceptic framing of CCS in a peer resource economy that Australian CCS advocacy will need to answer.

headline: US carbon capture 45Q tax-credit claims face long delays and rejections
summary: Accounting Today reports that claims for the US 45Q carbon-capture tax credit are encountering lengthy processing delays and rejections, adding uncertainty for project developers.
co2crc_note: 45Q execution friction is a cautionary data point on the gap between headline incentives and delivered support.
extractor_note: Radar / near-miss: published 6 Aug 2026, one day outside the 7-10 Aug window.

headline: Southeast Asia's race to become the region's CO2 storage hub
summary: A Pipeline Journal analysis examines how Indonesia, Malaysia and neighbours are competing to anchor cross-border CO2 storage and the pipeline and shipping infrastructure it requires.
co2crc_note: APAC storage-hub competition shapes the regional market Australia's export-storage ambitions sit within.
extractor_note: Radar / near-miss: published 6 Aug 2026, one day outside the 7-10 Aug window; analysis piece.
